title: Neural Network (MLP) From Scratch
summary: A fully connected multi-layer perceptron implemented with NumPy, including forward propagation, backpropagation, ReLU, Softmax, cross-entropy, and mini-batch gradient descent.
problem: Building a neural network without a deep-learning framework makes the learning loop impossible to hide. The project focuses on understanding how activations, gradients, loss, and parameter updates work together in a complete classifier.
approach: The implementation keeps the training path explicit: vectorized forward passes, backpropagation through ReLU layers, Softmax probabilities, cross-entropy loss, and mini-batch updates. It was trained for 26-class handwritten letter recognition.
limitations: The résumé records the recognition scope but does not provide a final accuracy, dataset name, or split protocol; those details should be added when verified.

title: Logistic Regression from Scratch
summary: Binary and multiclass logistic regression built from first principles with Softmax and cross-entropy, reaching 95.13% test accuracy.
problem: A compact classifier is useful only when the optimization and evaluation path are understandable. This project turns logistic regression into an inspectable implementation instead of a black-box estimator.
approach: The project implements binary and multiclass classification with vectorized NumPy operations, Softmax probabilities, cross-entropy loss, and gradient-based training. The reported result is a 95.13% test accuracy.
limitations: The résumé provides the test accuracy but not the dataset, class balance, split strategy, or baseline comparison; add those details before presenting this as a reproducible benchmark.

title: Linear Regression from Scratch
summary: A vectorized linear-regression implementation covering gradient descent, mean-squared-error cost, training, and performance visualization.
problem: Linear regression is simple enough to expose every part of an optimization loop: the cost surface, parameter updates, convergence behavior, and the relationship between predictions and error.
approach: The project implements gradient descent around a mean-squared-error objective, keeps training vectorized, and adds performance visualizations to make convergence and fit quality easier to inspect.
limitations: No quantitative benchmark was included in the résumé; add a verified dataset, error metric, and comparison baseline if this case study is expanded.
